feedback: Ordered-transition coverage fails at u3: the machine accepts target_room_entered (even without !has_matching_key semantics being the issue) and target_picked_up as terminal u4 reward, but 'u3, target_room_entered & !has_matching_key' as a single transition fires on a compound event; the target_picked_up case is fine, yet the real problem is that u3 -> u4 via target_room_entered skips rewarding the actual pickup, and FINAL_STATES u4 makes target_room_entered alone a terminal (reward 0.3) even though the task requires picking up the ball — accepting the episode's end at room entry breaks semantic fidelity. Additionally, if the agent picks up the ball from the doorway, target_room_entered and target_picked_up may coincide in one step and both transitions would be candidates, but that's minor. Critical issues: (1) terminal state u4 can be reached without target_picked_up, rewarding an unfinished task; (2) no dense per-step progress bounded to the task structure is missing — rewards are only on events (sparse), though this is tolerable if ordering is correct; (3) predicate-only events like key_found may fire simultaneously with others but the else self-loops cover irrelevant events, which is fine. Fix: require target_picked_up as the sole entry to a final accepting state, with target_room_entered as an intermediate state (u3 -> u4 on target_room_entered, u4 -> u5 on target_picked_up).
